question: On 30 November, around ten Israeli extremists attacked three Italian and one Canadian activist near Ein al-Duyuk1 in the West Bank in Palestine. The masked attackers (some of whom were armed) raided the building where the volunteers were sleeping and proceeded to strike them in the face, chest and other sensitive areas and steal some of their possessions, including identity papers and phones.

Incidents like this are testament to the increasingly violent tactics adopted by groups of extremist settlers, who have also stepped up their attacks in recent months. A number of sources have identified the Hilltop Youth as one of the groups most involved in planning and carrying out attacks for the purposes of intimidation2.

It should be kept in mind that this organisation is already listed under the EU Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime because of the serious human rights abuses it has committed3. Given the foregoing: 1.
Is the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy aware of the incident described above?

Given the Hilltop Youth’s organisational structure and the fact that it systematically plans and carries out violent attacks, is the VP/HR considering initiating the procedure to classify this entity as a terrorist group, a move that would be consistent with previous sanctions?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.2.2026) The EU strongly condemns the massive increase in settler violence, the policies and threats of forcible displacement and annexation in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. The EU has called on the Government of Israel to abide by its obligations under international law.

The EU has adopted sanctions under the EU Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime (EUGHRSR) against extremist settlers. The Council has so far listed nine individuals and five entities linked to violent extremism in Israel, the West Bank and the blocking of humanitarian aid to Gaza, including Hilltop Youth1.

In its conclusions of 18 December 2025, the European Council reiterated its call on the Council to take work forward on further restrictive measures against extremist settlers and entities and organisations that support them2. As regards the possibility of listing Hilltop Youth under the counterterrorism sanctions regime, such a decision would be subject to unanimity in the Council.

The legal prerequisite for a listing under Common Position 2001/931/CFSP (CP 931)3 on the application of specific measures to combat terrorism, is a competent authority decision, for example a Court decision or a proscription order by an administrative authority. Such a decision should concern the involvement of the entity in question in a terrorist act as defined by Article 1(3) of CP 931.
The practical effects of such a decision would be the same as those resulting from the listing under the EUGHRSR, namely an asset freeze.
